provisions.title: Access to patient information: charges and free copy for government benefits
provisions.citation: N.Y. Public Health Law 18(2)(e), as amended by L.2017, ch.322
provisions.quote: No charge may be imposed under this section for providing, releasing, or delivering patient information or copies of patient information where requested for the purpose of supporting an application, claim or appeal for any government benefit or program
provisions.appliesTo: "Health care provider" or "provider" means a "health care facility" or a "health care practitioner" as defined by this subdivision.

provisions.title: Access to patient information: copy furnished within a reasonable time
provisions.citation: N.Y. Public Health Law 18(2)(d), as amended by L.2024, ch.347
provisions.quote: upon the written request of any qualified person, a health care provider shall furnish to such person, within a reasonable time, a copy of any patient information requested
provisions.appliesTo: "Health care provider" or "provider" means a "health care facility" or a "health care practitioner" as defined by this subdivision.

leads.usedFor: Chapter 322 of 2017, free copies for benefits

copy_rights.note: Free copy for government benefit claims counts, beyond HIPAA and Part 171. Copies are due "within a reasonable time". Ten days applies to inspection, and to copies only where a practitioner lacks inspection space (18(2)(g)). Deadline element not counted.

reproductive.note: Limits subpoenas, including for records, tied to reproductive or gender-affirming care in out-of-state proceedings. Exceptions need patient-brought tort or contract claims, express consent, and an affirmation. Ch.694 signed 2025-12-19, effective immediately.

provisions.title: Confidentiality of genetic test records
provisions.citation: N.Y. Civil Rights Law 79-l(3)(a), as added by L.1996, ch.497
provisions.quote: All records, findings and results of any genetic test performed on any person shall be deemed confidential and shall not be disclosed without the written informed consent of the person to whom such genetic test relates.
provisions.appliesTo: Any person holding records or results of a genetic test

facts.statutoryDamages: None for individuals. GBL 899-aa(6): AG may recover actual costs or losses and civil penalties. CRL 79-l(5): civil fine up to $1,000; willful violation a misdemeanor, fine up to $5,000. PHL 2801-d(2): at least 25% of the daily per-patient rate per day of injury; punitive damages if willful or reckless.

provisions.quote: Any residential health care facility that deprives any patient of said facility of any right or benefit, as hereinafter defined, shall be liable to said patient for injuries suffered as a result of said deprivation, except as hereinafter provided.

Every patient shall have the right to have privacy in treatment and in caring for personal needs, confidentiality in the treatment of personal and medical records, and security in storing personal possessions.

private_right.note: No express private right of action found. GBL 899-aa(6) gives enforcement to the attorney general. CRL 79-l sets fines only. PHL 18 and 2782 name no personal action. S9269 is not law.

crossCheck.note: Level 1: limited to residential health care facility records. 2801-d last amended L.2022 ch.502, effective 2022-08-17. Minimum damages 25% of daily rate per day; punitive damages if willful. PHL 2783 and CRL 79-l give penalties only.
problems: Search missed PHL 2801-d, a private action for nursing home patients deprived of any statutory right, read with PHL 2803-c(3)(f), the right to confidentiality of medical records.
Status should be in_force, not no_law_found.
